scenes.headline: How Muon flattens every step it takes
scenes.sub: Momentum, orthogonalized by Newton-Schulz, for hidden 2D weights only.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Amber! Muon is an optimizer for the hidden layers of a network. It changes one thing about the update. Here's what, and why.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Before applying a hidden layer's momentum update, orthogonalize it: keep every direction, but give each the same size, so none dominates.
scenes.say: Before applying a hidden layer's momentum update, orthogonalize it. Keep every direction, but give each the same size, so none dominates.

scenes.title: Flatten the spectrum
scenes.say: Write the momentum update by its singular value decomposition.

parts.note: directions, and how far the step reaches along each
parts.say: Directions, and how far the step reaches along each one.

parts.note: a few huge values, the rest tiny: a lopsided step
parts.say: On real transformers, a few of those values are huge, so the step lurches along one direction.

parts.note: same directions, every value set to 1
parts.say: Muon keeps the directions and sets every value to one.

items.say: Add the gradient into a momentum buffer, as usual.
Divide by its norm, so every singular value sits between zero and one.
Apply a fixed quintic polynomial five times. It pulls every value toward one, and leaves the directions alone.
Apply the step. Embeddings, the output head, norms and biases stay on AdamW.

scenes.title: NanoGPT speedrun, ms per step
scenes.note: and Muon reaches the lowest validation loss fastest
scenes.say: It's nearly free. On the NanoGPT speedrun, a Muon step costs a hundred and forty-two milliseconds to Adam's hundred and thirty-nine, and reaches a lower loss sooner.

scenes.label: the compute Muon needs to match AdamW's loss, in Moonshot's fitted scaling law
scenes.note: with two fixes: weight decay, and update RMS matched to AdamW
scenes.say: At scale, Moonshot added weight decay and rescaled each update to AdamW's size. Their fitted curves say Muon matches AdamW with about half the compute.

scenes.text: Orthogonalizing the update is a cheap, well-motivated change that clearly helps hidden layers, and is nearly free per step.
scenes.say: So orthogonalizing the update is a cheap, well-motivated change. It clearly helps hidden layers, and it's nearly free per step.

recap: Keep the directions, equalize the sizes
Hidden 2D weights only; the rest on AdamW
scenes.say: To recap: equalize the step, do it with five cheap iterations, and only on hidden weight matrices.
